text: If you jumped into a hole straight through the Earth, you'd pop out the other side in thirty-eight minutes.
The deepest hole we ever actually dug is twelve kilometers. They gave up when the rock hit a hundred and eighty degrees.
So let's cheat. One tunnel, pole to pole, with all the air pumped out.
Within a minute, you've passed every hole humans ever dug.
And weirdly, gravity gets stronger as you fall, because you're closing in on the heavy iron core.
Thirteen minutes in, you're shooting through an ocean of liquid iron, as hot as the surface of the Sun.
At the center, you're doing over twenty-eight thousand kilometers an hour. And you weigh nothing at all.
Luckily, gravity now pulls you back and slows you down.
Unluckily, it stops you exactly at the far end, for about half a second.
Miss the edge, and you fall all the way home. Like a kid on a swing: fastest in the middle, stopped at each end.
Leave the air in, and drag holds you to two hundred kilometers an hour. After more than a day, you'd end up floating at the center of the Earth. Forever.
The plane is slower. But it has snacks.
